species.sourceFacts: Adult cleanerfish have a pale head, blue posterior and a black lateral stripe that broadens toward the tail. They occupy rocky or coral reefs and may clean larger client fish at a station. Museum sources report maximum total lengths of 11.5–12 cm.

sources.supports: identity, adult pattern, cleaning stations, 12 cm TL maximum and 2–40 m depth
posterior widening black stripe, reef habitat, 11.5 cm maximum

species.representedCues: continuous slender body; widening adult black stripe; rounded striped caudal fin; small paired pectorals
species.limits: Adult appearance only. Display-fin movement is authored, not measured locomotion; geometry alone does not implement client cleaning, parasites, sex change or social structure.

species.sourceFacts: A reef-associated porcupinefish with brown-grey upper surfaces, a pale belly, dark blotches edged in a pale colour, and unspotted fins. Museums Victoria reports a maximum size of 45 cm. The resting body here is not inflated, and its short spines remain laid back.

sources.supports: identity, pale-edged dark blotches, unspotted fins, reef association and 45 cm maximum
shorter spines compared with Diodon hystrix

species.representedCues: continuous thick but uninflated body; laid short spines; pale-edged dark blotches; unspotted rounded fins; no pelvic fins
species.limits: The outline, spine spacing and colours are authored interpretations, not calibrated anatomical measurements. No defensive inflation or crushing bite is simulated. Catalogue individual range is a selected display range rather than a museum population statistic.

species.sourceFacts: An Indo-Pacific reef predator with irregular reddish bands on a cream body, elongated dorsal spines, broad fan-like pectorals with rays beyond the membranes, and fleshy head appendages. Museums Victoria reports 38 cm TL and 1–128 m depth. These cues are used for recognition; the new geometry does not simulate prey capture or venom.

sources.supports: identity, irregular bands, long dorsal spines and projecting pectoral rays, head appendages, native Indo-Pacific habitat, 38 cm TL and 1–128 m

species.representedCues: continuous striped body; thirteen dorsal spines and basal membranes; two continuous bowed pectoral fans with projecting rays; small eye and head appendages; rounded spotted tail
species.limits: Fin motion is a restrained display approximation. Membranes are opaque double-sided surfaces for stable shared instancing, without measured underwater translucency. No hunting, venom, feeding event or complete ecological interaction is implied.

sharedResourcePolicy: one geometry kit per species and two materials per asset manager; repeated create returns independent fin transforms sharing geometry/material; dispose emits once per resource and is idempotent
performanceBudget: less than or equal to 9000 complete triangles per species before scene instancing
overallLimits: Species-distinct authored meshes, not documentary-quality scans, calibrated anatomy, photogrammetry or full food-web simulation. Local native mesh and resource checks do not prove WebGL frame rate or the visual result in a browser.
